Health Canada’s annual reports document the volume, growth, and Track 2 share of medical assistance in dying. This file is the accountability shelf for those numbers — and the door into the five-act argument under Rome Statute Article 6.
Hybrid stage: report film plus optional narration. Confirmed figures below cite Health Canada. Estimates beyond the last published report are labeled as estimates.

Some secondary summaries cite a higher running estimate after Dec 2024 by extrapolating daily rate. This page treats Health Canada’s published annual and cumulative tables as ground truth; open the report to verify.
Year-over-year growth into double digits for years after expansion; 2024 still rising, slower than the peak acceleration years.
This composite lives on the demographic board (MAID + opioids + intake + continuity). Open that page for labeled charts — not a substitute for Health Canada volume above.
Bill C-7 removed the reasonably foreseeable death safeguard. Intent and volume are argued in ACT I and ACT II.
Veterans Affairs offers, Foley, housing and palliative gaps — ACT III through V close the doctrine.
